title: Training the pixel art model for the new golden age of game dev!
author: HugoDzz
selftext:
Hey folks! We're two friends from computer graphics & machine learning. Here's our latest progress on a WIP pixel art model for sprite generation using some fancy techniques!  
  
These are 32x32 and 64x64, but the model can also do 16x16, 24x24, and 48x48.  
  
 We have a lot of ideas for improvements, up next!

comments.author: Ecstatic-Bend-104
comments.body:
Hey this is really neat! Your model visually honing in on the final output reminds me a bit of some work I’ve done previously training a CNN tensor flow model to interpolate subsurface geological surfaces from well data.

Can you speak to what the MLM is doing between prompt and final output, particularly in the first few frames of generation? How large is your training data sample size?

replies.author: HugoDzz
replies.body: We'll try to put a nice blog post to make a detailed walkthrough this! Basically here what you're seeing is the generation steps.

comments.author: RoyalSpecialist1777
comments.body: Hello!   How do you train it?  I like building models (including CNNs) but to get decent pixel art it seems like you will need quite a bit of training.  How much did it take?

replies.author: HugoDzz
replies.body: We'll put a writeup over this, but spoiler: it's a lot of training x) alongside new some techniques.

replies.author: RoyalSpecialist1777
replies.body:
Awesome.  New techniques are fun.    
  
I have been tinkering with pruning and normal feedforward networks where we process a domain specific corpus, find out which neurons consistently output close to 0 and don't impact downstream decisions, and thought it would be fun to try during training (where you turn unused ones off then periodically back on when there are errors and you need more neurons to encode more representations).  Neural networks are ridiculously inefficient.  But being an independent researcher there is only so much training I can do which would not be enough.   

Would love to have the resources.  Right now I use OSS 20B for tinkering and mechanistic interpretability stuff because it fits on my GPU.

The sprites look great.  I currently use gpt-image-2 for sprites, a game I am making on the side, but it generates high resolution drawings of sprites we have to then convert to pixels with Python and it just is clunky.  I tried a couple others from hugging face but those just were not very good.  Yours look neat.

replies.author: HugoDzz
replies.body: gpt image 2 is actually not bad, you can use a pixel snapper for making true pixel art. Buuut, still not there for my standard, so we're doing it ourselves, at the highest quality standard we want.
